guards.what: N: the power's sole applier is Flex Potion -- a PORTED potion, not a scope boundary (FlexPotion.cs:26-31 vs sts2_rl/potions.py:107-124)
guards.rationale:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-07-26 (potion-scope re-verdict pass), from waiver. The shared contract's 'Out of scope everywhere: potions (deferred by Perry)' has been DELETED on Perry's instruction ("don't ignore potions anymore"). `potion` is now an ordinary audit kind -- 51 sim units, audit/records/potion/, `harness.py roster potion` -- and it is UNAUDITED, exactly like `monster`. The previous pass had already narrowed this guard until the only thing left standing on the clause was 'there is no audit/records/potion/ tier for this potion to live in'. That sentence is no longer a scope statement, it is a coverage statement, and coverage is not a waiver. So the guard is re-derived on its merits: the applier potion is read in full against its C# model and verdicted here.
THE APPLIER IS FAITHFUL, AND THE ONE TRAP IN IT IS AVOIDED. src/Core/Models/Potions/FlexPotion.cs:22 declares CanonicalVars = new PowerVar<StrengthPower>(5m) -- note the var is typed on StrengthPower, but FlexPotion.cs:30 applies `PowerCmd.Apply<FlexPotionPower>(choiceContext, target, baseValue, base.Owner.Creature, null)`, i.e. the WRAPPER, with the StrengthPower var only supplying the number. Reading the var as the applied class would give plain permanent Strength instead of the end-of-turn-reverting temporary kind. sts2_rl/potions.py:121-124 applies FlexPotionPower with STRENGTH = 5 (sts2_rl/potions.py:117), so it takes the wrapper too. No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 5 is the pinned non-ascension value. APPLIER: C#'s fourth argument is `base.Owner.Creature` (parameter `Creature? applier`, src/Core/Commands/PowerCmd.cs:101), matching the sim's `applier=ctx.player`; cardSource is null on both sides. TargetType.AnyPlayer (FlexPotion.cs:20) and AssertValidForTargetedPotion (FlexPotion.cs:28) are the multiplayer target-validity path, waived as multiplayer; ExtraHoverTips (FlexPotion.cs:24) is presentation. Rarity Common (FlexPotion.cs:16) matches the sim's class default (sts2_rl/potions.py:34). REACHABILITY IS ESTABLISHED, NOT WAIVED (binding rule 6): @register_potion puts it in ALL_POTIONS and it is in the generation pool at sts2_rl/potion_pools.py:50 (common); the conformance runner asserts the belt slot by slot (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:625-631). WHAT IS STILL NOT JUDGED HERE is a coverage fact, not a verdict: `potion/flex_potion` has no record yet because the whole potion kind is unaudited. Nothing in this record depends on it.

It used to be recorded as a guard verdicted `waiver`, which was wrong: a tooling defect is not a scope exclusion, and binding rule 1 reserves `waiver` for genuinely out-of-scope material (multiplayer / presentation / ascension / other characters). It is a note about the audit apparatus, not a sim-vs-game finding, so it carries no verdict and does not enter this record's rollup.
